subject.title: Telegram: support fail-closed unknown-group handling with optional auto-leave

question: Should OpenClaw accept an opt-in Telegram unknown-group action config that can warn and leave non-allowlisted groups, using https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/50682 or a narrow successor as the implementation path?
rationale: The request adds new user-facing config plus an operator-controlled Telegram side effect in an authorization boundary, so automation cannot choose the permanent product/security contract.

options.title: Revise the linked Telegram PR
options.body: Use the existing implementation candidate, but require precise unknown-group classification, schema/docs alignment, native-command parity, cooldown handling, and real Telegram proof before merge.

options.title: Keep deny-only behavior
options.body: Decline warn/leave config for now and keep current fail-closed drop/log behavior plus Telegram platform controls as the supported posture.

options.title: Fold into broader group security work
options.body: Defer this narrow auto-leave behavior into the broader group pairing or cross-channel group-security direction tracked by related issues.

recommendation.title: Revise the linked Telegram PR
recommendation.body: Use the existing implementation candidate, but require precise unknown-group classification, schema/docs alignment, native-command parity, cooldown handling, and real Telegram proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision touches Telegram authorization, user-facing config, and security posture, and current routing/history best point to steipete for that product/security choice.
